graph.name: Toyota Cloud Lakehouse Architecture
graph.notes: Toyota's architecture converges on-premises data warehouses and domain data marts into a central lakehouse on AWS S3, utilizing EC2-hosted tools (Kafka, Talend, Databricks) for ingestion, Glue for metadata cataloging, RDS for processing metrics, and Redshift Spectrum and Athena for self-service querying.

nodes.name: On-Premises Systems
nodes.notes: Houses legacy data warehouses and domain data marts.

nodes.name: EC2 Ingestion Engines
nodes.notes: Hosts Kafka, Talend, and Databricks to process and ingest data securely over Direct Connect.

nodes.name: AWS Glue
nodes.notes: Stores catalog and metadata about incoming dataset schemas.

nodes.name: Amazon S3 Lakehouse
nodes.notes: Central data lake storing Source (SRC), Enterprise (ENT / DW), and Product (Prod / DM) data layers in Parquet and Delta formats.

nodes.name: Amazon RDS
nodes.notes: Stores ingestion processing metrics and execution status.

nodes.name: Amazon Redshift + Spectrum
nodes.notes: Provides a read-optimized data mart layer and uses Spectrum to query S3 directly.

nodes.name: Amazon Athena
nodes.notes: Enables serverless ad-hoc queries directly against S3 data.

nodes.name: Analysts / Data Scientists / Business Users
nodes.notes: End-user persona consuming data via self-service analytics and querying.

edges.notes: Data is securely transferred from on-premises systems into EC2-hosted ingestion engines over Direct Connect.
Ingestion engines pump processed data into S3 storage layers (Source, Enterprise, Product).
Ingestion processes register dataset catalog and schema metadata into AWS Glue.
Processing metrics and job logs are written to Amazon RDS.
Redshift and Redshift Spectrum read data from S3 for data mart workloads and cross-domain joins.
Athena queries raw and processed S3 data on the fly.
Redshift serves read-optimized data mart queries to analysts and business users.
Athena serves direct self-service queries to analysts, data scientists, and business users.
